Although studies in vitro found that iron (ferrous sulfate) caused a false-positive result in the Hemoccult test for blood in faeces, this did not occur in vivo in persons receiving oral iron therapy.1-3 An explanation for the difference in these findings was that hydrogen peroxide in the Hemoccult developer converted ferrous ions in solution to ferric ions, which caused oxidation in the test, whereas in vivo the iron was probably eliminated in the faeces in the form of non-reactive insoluble iron precipitates.2 1.
